chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hajjāl, from Ṣafwān ibn Mihrān, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the location of the grave of the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him). He said, so he described its location to me as being about a mile away. He said, so I went to it and prayed near it. Then I returned to Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) the following day and informed him of my going and my praying near it. He said, 'You were correct.' So I remained for twenty years praying near it.
ai.seo_question: What is the location of the grave of Imam Ali (a.s.) according to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.)?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the scholarly practice of verifying the location of Imam ‘Alī’s (a.s.) grave through direct confirmation by Imam al-Ṣādiq (a.s.), reflecting the Shia emphasis on the sanctity of the Ahl al-Bayt’s resting places. The narrator’s twenty-year devotion at this specific site underscores the spiritual merit of *ziyarat* (visitation) and serves as a foundational text for the traditional belief in the hidden yet accessible nature of the Imam’s tomb in Kufa.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 12. My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Nasr, who said:

I asked Imam Riďā (a.s.) about the location of the grave of the Commander of the Believers (a.s.). He told me that it was in Gharī. I asked, “May I sacrifice myself for you! Some people say that he is buried in Ruḥbah.” Imam (a.s.) replied, “No. Some people (even) believe that he is buried in the Mosque (of Kūfah).”
